text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, A21, A22 and A23 each appear in about 25 in 100 traces (49 of 200), down from about 75 in 100 (about 150 of 200) before. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- In the later window, A24, A25 and A26 each appear in about 76 in 100 traces (about 151 of 200), up from about 25 in 100 (about 50 of 200) before. [OCC006, OCC007, OCC008]
- A20's outgoing transitions are redirected: before, about 75% of them led to A21, A22 or A23 and about 25% to A24, A25 or A26; in the later window this is roughly reversed (about 24% versus about 75%). [DIR003]
- The two groups rarely occur together in either window, and the dominant side flips: for example, A21 occurs without A24 in about 74 in 100 traces before but about 25 in 100 later, while A24 occurs without A21 in about 25 in 100 before but about 76 in 100 later. Co-occurrence within each group follows the same flip (A21–A22 together 0.75 to 0.245; A24–A25 together 0.25 to 0.755), and A20 itself now usually appears without A21/A22/A23 and together with A24/A25/A26, the reverse of before. [REL015, REL022, REL028, REL013, REL021, REL034, REL039, REL007, REL010]
- Downstream partners switch association: A30 co-occurs with A21/A22/A23 in about 75 in 100 traces before versus about 25 in 100 later, and with A24/A25/A26 in about 25 before versus about 76 later; A32 and A33 shift away from the first group (co-occurrence about 0.48 to 0.15) toward the second (about 0.17 to 0.52). [REL018, REL031, REL036, REL040, REL019, REL037]
- Secondary changes rest on few observations: A10 appears in 42 of 200 later traces versus 11 before, its outgoing transitions concentrate on A33 (about 90% in the later window) and it occurs later within traces (mean relative position about 0.57 to 0.82); A32 now sends about 20% of its outgoing transitions to A10 (about 1% before); A02 is observed in only 2 later traces versus 18 before, with only 2 outgoing transitions observed after (to A15 and A27). [OCC002, POS001, DIR002, DIR004, OCC001, DIR001]
- Event-position gaps widen slightly around the growing group: A20→A24 and A25→A30 gaps shift from mostly 1 step toward 2–3 steps, and the A32→A33 gap-1 share falls from about 0.56 to about 0.39. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that routing at A20 shifted between two alternative activity groups: in the later window roughly three-quarters of cases execute A24, A25 and A26 where previously roughly three-quarters executed A21, A22 and A23, with the two groups near-mutually exclusive in both windows. The change is shown directly in A20's outgoing transition shares and consistently across participation, within-group and cross-group co-occurrence, and the switched association of downstream activities A30, A32 and A33 [DIR003, OCC003, OCC006, REL013, REL015, REL034, REL018, REL036, REL019, REL037]. The number of flagged items (62 versus about 1 expected without a change) far exceeds what an unchanged process typically produces, and the largest shifts rest on about 150 versus 49 traces per window, beyond ordinary sampling variation; note, however, that the many relation items largely restate one underlying difference rather than confirming it independently [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL013, REL014, REL021].

Limitations: the shift is partial rather than complete — about a quarter of later cases still run A21/A22/A23, so both groups remain in use — and the evidence shows correlated participation plus A20's outgoing shares but cannot establish that the six activities hang on a single decision point at A20, nor why the shares moved. The secondary changes around A10, A02, A32 and A33 rest on few observations (A02's later profile on only 2 outgoing transitions, A10 on 11 versus 42 traces), so their nature and their connection to the main shift remain unclear, and unobserved edges there do not mean those edges are absent. Exact shares such as "three-quarters" are finite-sample estimates, and sampling differences in variant frequencies between the windows cannot be fully excluded, although the size and consistency of the main pattern make chance an unlikely explanation for it [DIR001, OCC001, OCC002, DIR004].
